summary: Defines the rsync URI scheme, a way to write a link that names a file or directory reachable through the rsync file synchronization protocol. It is published for information only and is not a standards-track specification.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC defines the rsync URI scheme for naming an rsync source or destination. It covers rsync over TCP and sets a default port when a URI does not include one.

questions: what is the rsync uri scheme
what is the default rsync port
what is the format of an rsync url
does the rsync uri support ssh
subtitle: The registration of rsync:// as a URI scheme for rsync sources and destinations.

tldr.problem: The rsync utility needed a registered way to represent an rsync source or destination as a URI.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC registers the provisional rsync scheme with a host, path and optional user and port, using TCP as the transport.
tldr.outcome: The default port is 873. The scheme does not cover rsync over SSH, and the RFC is Informational.

today: RFC 5781 is Informational and has no later obsoleting or updating RFC listed in the unit metadata.

sections.title: Purpose of the rsync URI
sections.content: The rsync utility provides incremental file transfer. RFC 5781 defines a URI scheme for identifying a source or destination used by the rsync application. It follows the general URI syntax and registration procedures referenced by the document.
sections.plainLanguage: The scheme gives rsync sources and destinations a standard URI form. An rsync application can use the URI to identify a transfer endpoint.

sections.title: URI Form and Meaning
sections.content:
The generic form is rsync://[user@]host[:PORT]/Source. It contains a host and path, with an optional user and port. It can identify either a source or a destination for the rsync application.

If the port is omitted, it defaults to 873. The scheme is for the rsync protocol using TCP; transports such as rsync over SSH are not supported by this URI scheme. The RFC registers it as provisional.
sections.plainLanguage: An rsync URI names a host and path, and may include a user and port. If no port is given, the default is 873; the scheme covers TCP, not rsync over SSH.

sections.title: Registration and Security
sections.content:
IANA registered the provisional rsync URI scheme using the template in the RFC. The document applies the general URI security considerations in RFC 3986, including reliability, malicious construction, sensitive information and semantic attacks.

The RFC says the scheme has no particularly unique security considerations. It does not cover security considerations for the rsync protocol itself.
sections.plainLanguage: The RFC applies general URI security concerns to rsync addresses. It does not describe the security of the rsync protocol itself.

references.text: Berners-Lee, T., Fielding, R. and L. Masinter, "Uniform Resource Identifier (URI): Generic Syntax", STD 66, RFC 3986, January 2005.
